name: Proper Ordered Sample Compression of Singletons
details: The proper order-compression number of the singleton class is the separating example between proper and improper order compression.
proof: Darnstädt--Doliwa--Simon--Zilles order the singleton hypotheses.  For the sample containing negative labels on all but one coordinate, the remaining singleton is the first compatible proper hypothesis only after all $n-1$ negatives are retained; any proper subsample instead reconstructs a later singleton inconsistent with one omitted negative label.  Thus every proper order scheme needs $n-1$.  Keeping those negatives gives the matching scheme.
